card.name: Time-period nouns like month, week, year
card.fires_on: Singular time-period nouns (month, week, year, decade) right after "the", "this", or "a", often before a phrase like "before delivery" or "since". It also fires when the noun is followed by a hyphen, as in "week-by-week" or "year-round".

modes.label: Period before an event
modes.description: A singular time noun after "the" that locates something relative to an event.
modes.example: exposure to SSRIs, particularly in the<< month>> before delivery, has been associated with a

modes.label: Period in a hyphenated compound
modes.description: A time noun that begins a hyphenated compound such as week-by-week or year-round.

modes.label: Period after this or a
modes.description: A time noun after "this" or "a" in general prose about a span of time.
modes.example: A<< week>> or two ago, we looked at bananas

card.writes: It promotes hyphen-suffix tokens like "-wide", "-long" and "-scale", which suggests it expects a hyphenated compound to follow the time noun.
card.plain: It lights up on words like week, month or year when they name a specific period, especially after "the" or "this".
